questionText:
OFFICIAL LEVY BALLOT
PLEASANTS COUNTY COMMISSION
SPECIAL ELECTION TO AUTHORIZE
ADDITIONAL LEVIES
A special election to authorize additional levies
for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July
1, 2028, July 1, 2029, July 1, 2030 and July 1,
2031 for emergency services, specifically the
Pleasants County Emergency Ambulance
Authority Inc., in the amount of $621,489
annually and $3,107,445 during the term of the
levy according to the Order of the County
Commission entered on the 24th day of August,
2026.
That the additional rate of levy in cents per one
hundred dollars of assessed valuation on each
class of property shall be:
Class I – 3.10 cents
Class II – 6.20 cents
Class III – 12.40 cents
Class IV – 12.40 cents

subjectQuote: Monongalia County emergency medical services levy
questionText:
OFFICIAL LEVY BALLOT
MONONGALIA COUNTY COMMISSION
SPECIAL ELECTION TO AUTHORIZE
ADDITIONAL LEVY
Election to authorize a levy for the fiscal years
beginning July 1, 2027, 2028, 2029, and 2030
for the purpose of contributing funds from such
levy for emergency medical services for the
acquisition of equipment and other capital
improvements, payment of a portion of general
operating, maintenance, and other expenses in
the amount of approximately $5,345,131
annually and $21,380,524 during the term of
the Levy. The need for such funding has been
determined by the Order of the County
Commission of Monongalia County, West
Virginia entered on the 19th day of August
2026.
The additional levy for each one hundred
dollars assessed valuation of property for each
of the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July
1, 2028, July 1, 2029, and July 1, 2030, shall
be:
CLASS I properties 2.40 cents
CLASS II properties 4.80 cents
CLASS Ill properties 9.60 cents
CLASS IV properties 9.60 cents

questionText:
Special Levy Election
Historical Preservation Alliance
According to the Order of the Harrison County Commission, adopted on the 31st day of August, 2026, A Special election will be held to authorize
additional levies, allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount, for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029 and July 1,
2030 for the purpose of providing funding for the following organization in the following amounts:
Agency Fiscal Year 27/28 Fiscal Year 28/29 Fiscal Year 29/30 Fiscal Year 30/31
Historical Preservation Alliance $100,000 $103,000 $106,090 $109,272
Totals $100,000 $103,000 $106,090 $109,272
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027, shall be on Class I property 0.06 cents; on
Class II property 0.12 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 0.24 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2028, shall be on Class I property 0.06 cents; on
Class II property 0.12 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 0.24 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2029, shall be on Class I property 0.06 cents; on
Class II property 0.12 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 0.24 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2030, shall be on Class I property 0.07 cents; on
Class II property 0.14 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 0.28 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
That in the event the separate and aggregate assessed valuation of each class of taxable property within the County of Harrison increases during the
term of the special levy, the levy rate shall be adjusted so that the projected tax collection will not exceed the maximum sum of: $100,000 for the
fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027; $103,000 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2028; $106,090 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2029; and
$109,272 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2030.
Examples of authorized uses of levy funds are as follows: General operating expenses, building, infrastructure, and equipment maintenance and
repairs, promotion of tourism and historical preservation, acquisition and upgrades of equipment, property or structures, improvements and
modifications to land and facilities, and matching funds to obtain federal funds or other available funds. The Harrison County Commission will each
year provide the amount of funds from the levy to the Historical Preservation Alliance in the amounts as set forth in this order. Further, in relation to
the expenditure of funds, the Historical Preservation Alliance shall quarterly account for all expenditures, costs, and requisitions to the Harrison
County Commission; and no levy funds shall be distributed to the Historical Preservation Alliance without written proof being provided to, and
reviewed by, the Harrison County Commission. The Historical Preservation Alliance shall reimburse the Harrison County Commission for any and all
levy funds determined to have been expended for an unauthorized purpose.
In the event the Historical Preservation Alliance would cease to exist, for whatever reason, or, if the amount of funds collected exceed the
approximate amount, the Harrison County Commission will follow all necessary legal and governmental requirements to ensure that any funding
previously allocated to said entity may be repurposed; and that such finding may be repurposed for use in county special and/or improvements
projects; or otherwise that such funds be eliminated from collection consistent with West Virginia law.

subjectQuote: Community health, libraries and county special projects levy
questionText:
Special Levy Election
Community Health Organizations within Harrison County
Lowe Public Library, Southern Area Public Library, Nutter Fort Public Library
Harrison County Commission for Harrison County Special Projects
According to the Order of the Harrison County Commission, adopted on the 31st day of August, 2026, A Special election will be held to authorize
additional levies, allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount, for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029 and July 1,
2030 for the purpose of providing for the continued operation of the following organizations in the following amounts:
Agency Fiscal Year 27/28 Fiscal Year 28/29 Fiscal Year 29/30 Fiscal Year 30/31
Community Health $880,000 $906,400 $933,592 $961,600
Lowe Public Library $10,000 $10,300 $10,609 $10,927
Southern Area Public Library $10,000 $10,300 $10,609 $10,927
Nutter Fort Public Library $10,000 $10,300 $10,609 $10,927
Harrison County Special Projects $450,000 $463,500 $477,405 $491,727
Totals $1,360,000 $1,400,800 $1,442,824 $1,486,108
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027, shall be on Class I property 0.88 cents; on
Class II property 1.76 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 3.52 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2028, shall be on Class I property 0.91 cents; on
Class II property 1.82 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 3.64 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2029, shall be on Class I property 0.94 cents; on
Class II property 1.88 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 3.76 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
The additional levy allowing for 5% delinquencies and 2% discount for fiscal year beginning July 1, 2030, shall be on Class I property 0.96 cents; on
Class II property 1.92 cents; and on Class III and Class IV property 3.84 cents; per $100.00 valuation.
That in the event the separate and aggregate assessed valuation of each class of taxable property within the County of Harrison increases during the
term of the special levy, the levy rate shall be adjusted so that the projected tax collection will not exceed the maximum sum of: $1,360,000 for the
fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027; $1,400,800 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2028; $1,442,824 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2029; and
$1,486,108 for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2030.
Examples of acceptable usage of funds are as follows: General operating expenses, building, infrastructure, and equipment maintenance and
repairs, acquisition and upgrades of equipment, property or structures, improvements and modifications to land and facilities, and matching funds to
obtain federal funds or other available funds. The Harrison County Commission will each year provide the amount of funds from the levy to the
Clarksburg/Harrison Health Department, Lowe Public Library, Southern Area Public Library, Nutter Fort Public Library, and Harrison County for
Harrison County Special Projects. Funds for the remaining organizations will be distributed by the Clarksburg/Harrison Health Department to each
organization in the amounts as set forth in this order.
In the event any of these entities would cease to exist, for whatever reason, or, if the amount of funds collected exceed the approximate amount, the
Harrison County Commission will follow all necessary legal and governmental requirements to ensure that any funding previously allocated to said
entity may be redistributed to one or more of the remaining entities, on an equitable basis. If the amount of funds collected is less than the
anticipated approximate amount, each beneficiarys distribution amount will be reduced equitably.
In the event that sufficient State, Federal, or other special funds become available to provide monies for any of the above purposes, or the Harrison
County Commissions anticipated expenses for each stated purpose are lower than projected, the levy monies specified for these purposes may be
used for the general operation and improvement of the county. The Harrison County Commission is hereby authorized and empowered to expend,
during the term of this Levy, the funds, if any, occurring in excess of the amount needed for any of the above stated purposes for the enrichment,
supplementation, improvement and advancement of all county programs, operations and facilities in Harrison County, and other purposes pertinent
to the operation of the county.

subjectQuote: Hampshire County emergency medical services levy
questionText:
OFFICIAL LEVY BALLOT
Election to authorize additional levies for the
fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027; July 1, 2028;
July 1, 2029; July 1, 2030; and July 1, 2031, for
the provision, continuation, maintenance,
improvement, and expansion of countywide
emergency medical services, including
operations, staffing, training and workforce
development, vehicles, equipment, supplies,
facilities, administration, community EMS
education and training, and lawful support for
qualifying community emergency medical
services providers and recognized EMS
response partners serving Hampshire County,
according to the Order of the County
Commission of Hampshire County entered on
the 11th day of August, 2026.
The approximate net annual amount for the
stated purpose is $2,173,478.
The additional levy shall be on Class I property
4.75 cents; on Class II property 9.50 cents; on
Class III property 19.00 cents; and on Class IV
property 19.00 cents per $100 of assessed
value. The County Commission may reduce, but
shall not increase, these rates in any year if
reduced rates will meet projected needs.
Instructions: those favoring the additional Levy
fill in the oval FOR THE LEVY; those against the
Levy fill in the oval AGAINST THE LEVY.

questionText:
OFFICIAL LEVY BALLOT
BOARD OF EDUCATION OF
THE COUNTY OF JACKSON
NOVEMBER 3, 2026
Special election to authorize additional levies for
the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2029; July 1,
2030; July 1, 2031; July 1, 2032; and July 1,
2033; for the purposes set forth as follows:
1. That the purposes for which additional
funds are needed and the annual approximate
amount for such purposes after due allowances
for exonerations, delinquencies, etc., are as
follows:
A. To provide funds to repair, improve, and
maintain the existing Board owned motor
vehicles and where necessary to purchase new
and additional motor vehicles in order to facilitate
a safe and efficient school system at the rate of
five percent (5%) of the total annual additional
levy proceeds, for an approximate annual cost of
$688,380
B. To provide funds to distribute free
textbooks and workbooks to all students in the
Jackson County School District, and to supply
and equip elementary and secondary schools at
the rate of ten percent (10%) of the total annual
additional levy proceeds, for an approximate
annual cost of $1,376,760
C. To provide funds to repair, improve, add
to, and maintain all school facilities, to defray
utility costs, and to provide funds for land and for
the construction of buildings thereon or upon any
land now owned by the Board of Education at
the rate of twenty-five percent (25%) of the total
annual additional levy proceeds, for an
approximate annual cost of $3,441,901
D. To provide funds for the employment of
additional school system personnel to meet the
needs of the school system and to maintain
and/or increase the present supplement to the
state basic salary scale and provide benefits for
all school personnel at the rate of sixty percent
(60%) of the total annual additional levy
proceeds, for an approximate annual cost of
$8,260,563
2. That the total approximate amounts
needed during the term of this five-year (5) levy
after due allowances for exonerations,
delinquencies, etc., for said purposes is
approximately $68,838,020
All according to the order of the Board of
Education of the County of Jackson entered on
the 23rd day of July, 2026.
The additional levy shall be on Class I
property 22.95 cents; on Class II property 45.90
cents; on Class III property 91.80 cents; and on
Class IV property 91.80 cents. Such additional
levies shall be based on each one hundred
dollars valuation of Classes I, II, III, and IV
property.

OFFICIAL LEVY BALLOT
General Election on November 3, 2026 to Authorize
Additional Levies According to the Order of
The Board of Education of the County of Mason
Adopted and Entered on August 11, 2026
Special election to authorize additional levies (the "Excess Levy") for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2029, July 1, 2030, July 1, 2031, July 1, 2032, and July 1,
2033 in the approximate average amount of $9,923,215 annually for the purpose of the payment of the general current expenses of The Board of Education of the
County of Mason (the "Board"), including for the purposes hereinafter set forth; all according to the Order of the Board entered on the 11th day of August, 2026, and
as more particularly described below.
PURPOSE FOR WHICH ADDITIONAL FUNDS ARE NEEDED ANNUAL AMOUNT FOR EACH PURPOSE
Professional and Service Salary Supplements, Personnel Taxes and Benefits $3,000,000
- Including, but not limited to, school nurse health services above state aid funding,
supplemental salaries for dual credit courses, existing county supplements, salaries or
personnel in excess of 200 days, supplemental co-curricular and extracurricular salaries
(academic, arts, and athletic), staff attendance incentives, FICA taxes, unemployment taxes,
workers' compensation taxes, and/or retirement, dental and/or vision insurance.
Textbooks, Supplies, and Equipment and Insurance - Including, but not limited to, free $1,400,000
textbooks and textbook-related materials, duplicating paper, computer paper, writing paper,
notebook paper, instructional supplies and equipment, including library, office operating expenses
and/or accident insurance for all county students during school and school related activities.
Extra and Co-Curricular activities - Including, but not limited to, field trips, school competitions, $450,000
free admission for secondary students into their home school activities, free sports passes
available to veterans, first responders and senior citizens with appropriate identification,
and/or other extra and co-curricular expenses.
Construction and Repair, Maintenance and Building Utilities - Including, but not limited to, $2,942,594
construction, building repairs, roof replacement, asbestos projects, structural repairs, fire code
corrections, Americans with Disabilities Act compliance, equipment maintenance, paving, safety and
security systems, lawn maintenance, lease purchases and/or all utilities and utility-related costs.
Computer Technology - Including, but not limited to, technician salaries and related benefits, $150,000
computer purchases, repair, upgrades, software, and/or contracting.
Student Transportation - Including, but not limited to, maintenance of equipment, vehicle $633,121

Special Levy Election
to Authorize the Additional Levies
According to the Order of The Board of Education
of the County of Hardy Adopted and Entered on August 19, 2026
Special election to authorize additional levies (the “Excess Levy”) for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029, July 1, 2030,
and July 1, 2031, in the approximate average amount of $1,300,459 annually, for the purpose of the payment of the general current expenses of The
Board of Education of the County of Hardy (the “Board”), including for the purposes hereinafter set forth; all according to the Order of the Board
entered on the 19th day of August, 2026, and as more particularly described below.
The purpose for which additional funds are needed during the term of this five-year levy, and the approximate average annual amount for such
purpose after due allowances for discounts, delinquencies, exonerations, uncollected taxes and shrinkage, subject to variation from year to year, are
as follows:
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
PURPOSE FOR WHICH ANNUAL AMOUNT FOR
ADDITIONAL FUNDS ARE NEEDED EACH PURPOSE__________________
Employment and Retention Support, including, without
limitation, funding to maintain current and additional
needed positions above the funding formula provided by the
state, to improve and enhance the Hardy County School $1,300,459
District’s instructional program, school safety and/or
student support programs by the employment and retention
of qualified teachers and/or service personnel.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
The amount set forth above is the anticipated average annual amount for this purpose. The actual amount likely will vary from one fiscal year to the
next. If the above-stated purpose is declared unconstitutional or invalid due to judicial or legislative action, then any affected funds may be used for
the enrichment, supplementation, operation, and improvement of educational services, schools and/or facilities in the public schools of Hardy County,
West Virginia, as Board may determine from time to time, in its discretion.
The total amount necessary to carry out the above purpose over five fiscal years, after making reasonable allowances for discounts, delinquencies,
exonerations, uncollected taxes and shrinkage, is $6,502,295 or the average sum of $1,300,459 annually. The actual amount budgeted, as well as
the amount spent, for such purpose likely will vary from one fiscal year to the next depending on the realized tax collections and the needs of the
Hardy County School District, as determined by the Board with respect to each fiscal year. If the amount budgeted by the Board for a fiscal year are
not able to be spent entirely in such fiscal year, then the unspent amount shall be carried over and, in the Board’s sole discretion, spent on such
specific purpose in subsequent fiscal years.

may be used, solely or on a matching basis, to secure said additional funds or provide additional services. Additional funds received by grant,

eleven, of the West Virginia Code.

West Virginia, including student instructional supplies, materials, equipment, facility improvements and/or capital projects, as Board may determine
from time to time, in its discretion.

total of any such reduction shall not exceed the amount of such collection shortfall each year.

cents; on Class III property 15.16 cents; on Class IV property 15.16 cents.

July 1, 2030 and July 1, 2031.

Those favoring the additional levies, mark in the square "FOR THE LEVIES"; and those against such additional levies, mark in square
"AGAINST THE LEVIES".

According to the Order of The Board of Education
of the County of Summers Adopted and Entered on July 28, 2026
Special election to authorize additional levies (the "Excess Levy") for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029, and July 1,
2030, in the approximate average amount of $1,141,835 annually, for the purpose of the payment of the general current expenses of The Board of
Education of the County of Summers (the "Board"), including for the purposes hereinafter set forth; all according to the Order of the Board entered on
the 28th day of July, 2026, and as more particularly described below.
The purposes for which additional funds are needed during the term of this four-year levy, and the approximate average annual amount for such
purposes after due allowances for discounts, delinquencies, exonerations, uncollected taxes and shrinkage, subject to variation from year to year,
are as follows:
PURPOSE FOR WHICH ADDITIONAL FUNDS ARE NEEDED ANNUAL AMOUNT FOR EACH PURPOSE
a. To provide supplemental funds for the hiring of teachers and school level
service personnel for student support and academic services. $500,000
b. To provide funds for curricular and extracurricular trip support. $75,000
c. To provide funds for playground renovations at Talcott Elementary School,
Hinton Area Elementary, and Jumping Branch Elementary School which
includes but not limited to equipment, fencing, ground surfacing. $100,000
d. To provide funds for a safe school entrance at Jumping Branch Elementary School. $100,000
e. To provide a yearly salary and fixed cost such as retirement, insurance,
social security and workers compensation (all required for employment) for a
School Resource Officer at Summers County Comprehensive High School for
a 9-month contract while school is in session. $65,000
f. To provide funds for facilities improvements, preventative maintenance,
additions, equipment, and/or renovations at various Summers County
Schools and/or the Transportation Garage. $221,835
g. To provide funds to update the transportation and maintenance vehicles
to better serve the county. $40,000
h. To provide funds for security window treatments and related improvements
at various Summers County Schools as an additional safety measure. $15,000
i. To provide funds for exterior lighting and related improvements at Summers
County Comprehensive High School. $25,000
The amounts set forth above are the anticipated average annual amounts for each purpose. The actual amounts for each purpose likely will vary
from one fiscal year to the next. If any item in the above-stated purposes is declared unconstitutional or invalid due to judicial or legislative action,
then any affected funds will be distributed among the remaining constitutional and valid itemized purposes.
The total amount necessary to carry out the above purposes over four fiscal years, after making reasonable allowances for discounts, delinquencies,
exonerations, uncollected taxes and shrinkage, is $4,567,340, or the average sum of $1,141,835 annually. If the amounts budgeted by the Board for
a specific purpose or purposes for a fiscal year are not able to be spent entirely in such fiscal year, then the unspent amounts shall be carried over
and, in the Board's sole discretion, spent on such specific purpose or purposes in subsequent fiscal years.
If additional State, Federal, private or other special funds are made available to the Board for any of the above-stated purposes, the amounts herein
set forth may be used, solely or on a matching basis, to secure said additional funds or provide additional services. Additional funds received by
grant, donation or otherwise from the state or federal government, or from any agency of either, or from any other public or private source, for the
above-stated purposes, may be used either in substitution for or in addition to the funds obtained from this Excess Levy.
To the extent permitted by then-existing law, the Board reserves unto itself as the levying body the right and authority, in its discretion, to reduce the
rates of the excess levy, should increased assessments produce funds in excess of projected needs in any year specified in the levy call in
accordance with section six-g, article eight, chapter eleven, of the West Virginia Code.
The Board is hereby authorized and empowered to expend, during the term of this Excess Levy and one additional year, the surplus, if any, accruing
in excess of the above amounts needed for any of the above-stated purposes, plus excess collections due to increased assessed valuations for the
enrichment, supplementation, operation, and improvement of educational services, schools and/or facilities in the public schools of Summers County,
West Virginia, including, without limitation, student instructional supplies, materials, equipment, facility improvements and/or capital projects, as
Board may determine from time to time, in its discretion.
In the event that the actual amount collected is less than the amounts noted for the above-stated purposes for any one or more fiscal years, the
Board is hereby authorized and empowered to determine, in its discretion, which one or more of the above-stated purposes shall be reduced for
each such fiscal year, and the amount of each such reduction for such fiscal year; provided, that the total of all such reductions shall not exceed the
amount of such collection shortfall each year.
The additional levy, in cents per $100 of assessed value on each class of property, shall be on Class I property 4.84 cents; on Class II property 9.68
cents; on Class III property 19.36 cents; on Class IV property 19.36 cents.
That the proposed years to which the additional rate of levies shall apply are the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2027, July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029, and
July 1, 2030.
INSTRUCTION TO VOTERS:
Those favoring the additional levies, fill in the oval next to "FOR THE LEVIES"; and those against such additional levies, fill in the oval next to
"AGAINST THE LEVIES".

questionText:
SPECIAL LEVY ELECTION
General Election on November 3, 2026 to Authorize
Additional Levies According to the Order of
The Board of Education of the County of Marshall
Adopted and Entered on July 14, 2026
Special election to authorize additional levies (the "Excess Levy") for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029, July 1, 2030, July 1, 2031,
and July I, 2032 in the approximate average amount of $52,018,500 annually for the purpose of the payment of the general current expenses of The
Board of Education of the County of Marshall (the "Board"), including for the purposes hereinafter set forth; all according to the Order of the Board
entered on the 14th day of July, 2026, and as more particularly described below.
The purposes for which additional funds are needed during the term of this five year levy, and the approximate average annual amount for such
purposes after due allowances for discounts, delinquencies, exonerations, uncollected taxes and shrinkage, subject to variation from year to year as
set forth herein, are as follows:
PURPOSE FOR WHICH ADDITIONAL FUNDS ARE NEEDED ANNUAL AMOUNT FOR EACH PURPOSE
A. To provide funding for the Project Lead The Way/ STEM / Robotics curriculum
grades K-12, including, without limitation, teacher positions and coaching positions. $250,000
B. To provide funding for counselors, including, without limitation, fringe benefits
across the county beyond the State funding formula. $400,000
C. To provide funding for nurses, including, without limitation, fringe benefits
throughout the county beyond the State funding formula. $400,000
D. To provide funding for Social Worker services to students, including, without
limitation, Community in Schools, up to three Social Workers and Independent
Therapy Services not funded through the State. $500,000
E. To provide funding for up to five Resource Officers at the High Schools and Middle
Schools and up to three Elementary security officers through the Marshall County Sheriff's
Office. These services may be utilized in both our schools and for sporting event security. $800,000
F. To provide funding for intervention specialists, including, without limitation, fringe
benefits across the county elementary schools and up to five Reading
Specialists/lnterventionalists. $500,000
G. To provide funding for Community Activity Passes for Marshall County Schools events. $150,000
H. To provide funding for summer school for remediation, enrichment and CTE camp,
including, without limitation, personnel and supplies. $200,000
I. To provide funding for Grand Vue Leadership Camp Scholarships for Marshall County Students. $200,000
J. To provide funding for Back to School Fair and Parent Education Resource Center. $60,000
K. To provide funding for free breakfast, lunch, and summer feeding to students in the County. $500,000
L. To provide funding for vehicle maintenance, fuel and/or bus replacements. $1,500,000
M. To provide funding to library services through the "Moundsville-Marshall County
Public Library" (Public/County Libraries of Benwood, Cameron and Moundsville). $250,000
N. To provide funding to the Marshall County 4-H through the WVU Extension Service. $75,000
0. To provide funding to the Marshall County Health Department for county-wide health services. $100,000
P. To provide funding to create and sustain a School-Based Health Clinic for Marshall County
Students and Employees. $250,000
Q. To provide funding for contracts across the County for the Pre-Kindergarten Program. $300,000
R. To provide funding for various renovations, capital improvements and/or new
construction projects throughout the County. $21,520,335
S. To provide funding for school safety and security upgrades, including, without
limitation, security cameras. $20,000
T. To provide funding for improved access to technology throughout the County,
including, without limitation, the purchase of hardware, software, infrastructure, repairs,
training, and/or tech support personnel. $1,500,000
U. To provide funding for the maintenance and repair of equipment and buildings throughout
the County, including, without limitation, extended employment for summer maintenance. $3,000,000
V. To provide funding for supplemental special education services for certain identified
students beyond the State funding formula. $500,000
W. To provide funding portions of employee salaries and benefits, including, without
limitation, the local county salary supplements, fixed charges, dental and optical plans,
stipends, and/or Medical Benefit Cards expenses. $16,018,165
X. To provide funding for vocational supplies, equipment and personnel, including,
without limitation, up to twenty-four teachers that are employed in the County but
are not funded through the State formula. $500,000
Y. To provide funding for music, band and/or strings equipment. $125,000
Z. To provide funding for the purchase of instructional equipment, teaching supplies,
textbooks, and/or library books. $1,500,000
AA. To provide funding for extended day learning, including, without limitation, personnel and supplies. $200,000
BB. To provide funding for extra duty salary supplements for curricular positions and athletic coaches. $700,000
TOTAL: $52,018,500
As noted above, the amounts set forth above are the average annual amounts for each purpose. The actual amounts for each purpose likely will vary
from one fiscal year to the next. If any item in the above-stated purposes is declared unconstitutional or invalid due to judicial or legislative action,
then any affected funds will be distributed among the remaining constitutional and valid itemized purposes. The actual amounts budgeted, as well as
the amounts spent, for each purpose and in aggregate, likely will vary from one fiscal year to the next depending on the realized tax collections and
the needs of the Marshall County School District, as determined by the Board with respect to each fiscal year. If the amounts budgeted by the Board
for a specific purpose or purposes for a fiscal year are not able to be spent entirely in such fiscal year, then the unspent amount may be carried over
and spent on such specific purpose or purposes in subsequent fiscal years.
If additional State, Federal, private or other special funds become available to provide funding for any of the above-stated purposes, or if surplus
funds are generated due to increased assessed valuations, then in either case the Board shall be authorized and empowered to expend at the end of
each fiscal year, during the term of the levies, the surplus (if any) in excess of the amount needed for any of the above-stated purposes for the
enrichment, supplementation and advancement of all educational programs in Marshall County, and other purposes pertinent to the operation of
Marshall County Schools, in the discretion of the Board. Such additional or surplus funds may be used either in substitution for or in addition to the
funds obtained from the Excess Levy.
In the event that the actual amount collected is less than the approximate annual amounts allocated for the above-stated purposes for any one or
more fiscal years (including, without limitation, as a result of any amendments to the West Virginia Constitution or changes the Code of West Virginia
impacting property taxes, levy rates or similar matters), the Board is hereby authorized and empowered to determine in its discretion (i) which one or
more of the above-stated purposes shall be reduced for each such fiscal year, and (ii) the amount of each such reduction for such fiscal year;
provided, however, that the total of all such reductions shall not exceed the amount of such collection shortfall each year.
In the event that a specific library or school facility that is named in the above-stated purposes closes or otherwise ceases operation, the Board, in its
sole discretion, may reallocate funds that were originally allocated to those specific library or school facilities to any of the other above-stated
purposes. The Board will not issue bonds in connection with the approval of the proposed Excess Levy.
The Board reserves unto itself as the levying body the right and authority to reduce the rates of the excess levy, in its sole discretion, if increased
assessments would produce funds beyond projected needs in any fiscal year specified in the levy call.
The additional levies, in cents per $100 of assessed value on each class of property, shall be on Class I property 20.66 cents; on Class II property
41.32 cents; on Class III property 82.64 cents; and on Class IV property 82.64 cents.
That the proposed years to which the additional rate of levies shall apply are the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2028, July 1, 2029, July 1, 2030, July
1, 2031, and July 1, 2032.
INSTRUCTION TO VOTERS:
Those favoring the additional levies, fill in the oval "FOR THE LEVIES"; and those against such additional levies, fill in the oval "AGAINST THE
LEVIES".

OFFICIAL LEVY BALLOT
OFFICIAL BALLOT
THE BOARD OF EDUCATION OF THE COUNTY OF WIRT
GENERAL ELECTION HELD TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2026
Shall The Board of Education of the County of Wirt (the “Board”) incur debt and issue Bonds, in one or more series, in the par amount of not more
than NINE MILLION THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS ($9,300,000), with maturities on such Bonds to run not more than fifteen and
one-half (15.5) years from the date of such Bonds, with interest not exceeding the rate of five and three-quarters percent (5.75%) per annum,
payable semi-annually, for the purpose of making the following improvements in the Wirt County School District (estimated costs to include both the
Bond proceeds and proceeds of grants, if any, received from the School Building Authority of West Virginia and other sources, including but not
limited to Federal, State, local, lease purchase, and/or private funds) to provide adequate, safe and convenient educational facilities for the Wirt
County School District (the “School District”), and levy taxes sufficient to pay the interest on and the principal of such Bonds.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
PROJECT LOCATION ESTIMATED COST ESTIMATED COST
Funded by SBA/Other Sources* Funded by Bond Proceeds
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
New Additions, Improvements and Existing campus $18,000,000 $5,200,000
Renovations to Wirt County High School of Wirt County High School,
Elizabeth, West Virginia
Develop, acquire, design, construct, equip, demolish, furnish, improve, and pay all fees and expenses in connection with renovations and new
additions to Wirt High School, including, without limitation, new academic space, a kitchen, an auxiliary gym and/or supporting areas. The existing
classroom building will be demolished, and areas connecting new to the renovated parts of the building will be retained and renovated. The existing
annex building and surrounding area will be remodeled and expanded to add support spaces for the football field, including, without limitation,
enlarged toilets, a new concession stand, a ticket booth, and/or a visitors’ locker room. The project will meet the School Building Authority of West
Virginia standards and guidelines and provide asafe and engaging learning environment for students. The high school will serve students in grades
9 through 12.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Athletic Field Improvements to Wirt County Existing campus $3,000,000
High School of Wirt County High School,
Elizabeth, West Virginia
Develop, acquire, design, construct, equip, furnish, improve, and pay all fees and expenses in connection with improvements to the Wirt County High
School athletic field, including, without limitation, renovated bleachers, a new press box and/or the addition of a practice track.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
New Bus Garage Palestine, West Virginia $900,000
Develop, acquire, design, construct, equip, furnish, improve, and pay all fees and expenses in connection with a new bus garage shell building
and/or related improvements.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Total Estimated Project Cost (including Costs of Issuance): $27,300,000
Estimated Project Costs Funded by Other
Sources, including SBA Grants or Other
Available Funds*: $18,000,000
Project Costs Funded by Bond Proceeds: $9,100,000
Estimated Costs of Issuance: $200,000
TOTAL PAR AMOUNT OF BONDS: $9,300,000_______
* The Estimated Project Costs Funded by Other Sources may be an amount greater or less than $18,000,000, depending on the amount of any
commitment by the School Building Authority of West Virginia or other sources, final designs, plans and specifications of the respective Projects and
actual costs of construction of the Projects. The amounts set forth above as “Total Par Amount of Bonds” for the Projects include estimated Costs of
Issuance for the Bonds, which may be funded from the proceeds of the Bonds. The Board shall also be authorized to pay such Costs of Issuance
from its general funds and/or the proceeds of the Bonds, as the Board deems appropriate at the time such Costs of Issuance are required to be paid.
The issuance of the Bonds (i) is subject to (a) the School Building Authority of West Virginia’s award or commitment of funds to the Board in amounts
sufficient, in the Board’s reasonable discretion, to undertake and complete the Projects, and/or (b) the availability of other funds to the Board
(including federal, state, local, lease purchase proceeds and/or private funds from any source or any combination thereof), in amounts sufficient, in
the Board’s reasonable discretion, to undertake and complete the Projects, and (ii) is further subject to any and all other necessary actions,
approvals and consents required by applicable law.
The foregoing estimated Project Cost amounts include the costs of acquiring any necessary lands, sites and rights-of-way and easements, if
necessary to complete the Projects, the payment of interest on the Bonds while the Projects are under construction and up to six months thereafter,
and any engineering and architectural costs, construction costs, including, but not limited to, construction manager fees and expenses, the cost of
using county maintenance personnel, the costs of erecting, improving, equipping and furnishing the Projects, the costs and estimated costs of the
issuance of the Bonds, and such other costs, fees, and expenses as may be necessary and/or properly incurred in carrying out the Projects. All
Handicapped and E.S.S.I.A. Title I expenditures are subject to written approval by the West Virginia Department of Education.
The estimated Project Costs set forth above are based upon the estimates provided to the Board by its architects, engineers and other professional
advisers, and the actual costs of completing any one or more of the Projects may vary due to circumstances beyond the reasonable control of the
Board. To the extent the actual cost to complete any one or more of the Projects is greater or less than such estimates, the Board, in its reasonable
discretion, can allocate and expend the available funds (including proceeds of the Bonds, School Building Authority of West Virginia grant funds and
other funds available to the Board) between the Projects as necessary to carry out the intent of this Order; provided, however, that in any event, the
Board shall use its best efforts to complete each of the Projects described above, to the extent sufficient funding is available. If the proceeds of the
Bonds and/or amounts allocated for the above-stated purposes are insufficient to complete the Projects, then the Board, in its discretion, shall
allocate such shortfall to one or more of the above-stated purposes. In the event the Board shall obtain additional money by grant or otherwise from
the State or Federal government, or from any agency of either, or from any other source (including private funds, local funds, lease purchase
proceeds, or other funds made available to the Board), for use in the acquisition, construction, renovation, improvement, furnishing, and/or equipping
of the Projects, such additional money may be used either in substitution for or in addition to the proceeds of the sale of the Bonds proposed hereby,
as may be determined by the Board and the granting body or agency.
If the voters of the School District approve the incurring of said debt and the issuance of said Bonds, the Board will lay annually upon the assessed
valuation of all the taxable property within the School District an additional levy sufficient to provide funds for the payment of the annual interest upon
the Bonds as such interest accrues semiannually and the principal of the Bonds at maturity, for which purposes a levy upon each $100 valuation,
based upon the last assessment of such property for State and County purposes, will be required as follows:
Upon Class I Property approximately 11.09 cents
Upon Class II Property approximately 22.18 cents
Upon Class III Property approximately 44.36 cents
Upon Class IV Property approximately 44.36 cents
NOTICE TO VOTERS: To vote in favor of the proposition (for the Bond Issue) submitted on this ballot, mark an “X” in the box next to “
Yes”. To vote against the proposition (against the Bond Issue), mark an “X” in the box next to “No”.

questionText:
SPECIAL ELECTION TO AUTHORIZE
ADDITIONAL LEVIES
A special election to authorize additional
levies for the fiscal years beginning July 1, 2028;
July 1, 2029; July 1, 2030; July 1, 2031; July 1,
2032 (a period of five years), entered according
to the Order of the City of Richwood entered on
the 16th day of July 2026 for the purposes of
a.) Streets (funds for general repair of
existing streets, alleys, and storm drains)
b.) Fire Protection (for services related to
protection against loss by fire)
c.) Police Protection (for expenses related
to police protection)
That the additional rate of levy in cents per
one hundred dollars of assessed valuation on
each class of property shall be:
Class I 6.25 cents
Class II 12.50 cents
Class III *if any 25.00 cents
Class IV 25.00 cents
In the event the separate and aggregate
assessed value of each class of taxable property
within the City of Richwood increases during the
term of the special excess levy, the levy rate
shall be reduced so that the projected tax
collection will not exceed $75,000.00 in any
fiscal year.
